Thus I emended what is in M: ἐχενηΐδας ἀπλοίας [ship-holding calms]. To ἐχενηΐδας αὔρας [ship-holding breezes] the old commentator had added the gloss ἄπλοιαν [a calm], which gloss, when it had expelled the word αὔρας [breezes] which I restored as Aeschylus's, was changed into ἀπλοίας [calms], so that it might fit the plural adjectives ἀντιπνόους χρονίας ἐχενηΐδας [contrary, long-lasting, ship-holding].
